answer: Every agent identity must pay a small per-action fee that is escrowed in a shared kernel, and reputation only accrues when other agents attest the work was genuine. A sybil must therefore fund thousands of identities, each paying real coins per verified action, before any fake attestations count; the more identities it spins up, the more it must burn, and slashed bonds when collusion is detected remove the payoff. Honest agents absorb tiny fees that a lone worker can harbor, while an attacker faces costs scaling linearly with the swarm it needs to overcome the nebula of cross-checks.
